title: Sitting in, giving up clarinet, Rappolo's borrowed clarinet
summary: Mares sat in around Chicago and Biloxi but never became good enough; he kept the Albert clarinet Rappolo used on two recordings.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You went to Chicago in the early days. Tell me some more about your playing. You probably gave up clarinet.
Well, I used to go sit in with Charlie Cadela and Abby Bernstein at the halfway house and at the Paris Royal later when Abby played there.
Did you ever play professionally or just go around sitting in?

Well, in Biloxi. I played, I wouldn't say professional, but I used to sit in with Julian Lane and all the boys around up there. And, of course, Abby wasn't in Biloxi at that time, but he came over quite a bit and married. And I played with them, but I never really got to be able to play the clarinet like the greats, like Fazola and Rap. And stuff like
those fellas so I just threw it on the west side.

Oh yeah. In fact I still have it. You still have one? I still have the old Albert System clarinet that Rap used when he made She's Crying For Me blues and Golden Leaf Struts. Yes I have it because he used my clarinet. That time he didn't have any. I think he used Harry Shields' mouthpiece. But I had a chance anyhow to hear all the greats and that's one thing I'll always remember. Of course Brother Paul passed on.
